pr_title: Handle the case when zero byte reads are cancelled with an empty buffer
pr_body:
- When there's no buffer allocated and the zero byte reads is cancelled, it'll try to make a read only sequence with the current buffer, if that buffer is null because it wasn't yet allocated, it'll end up throwing a null reference exception. This adds a check to make sure were return an empty ReadOnlySequence if the backing buffer is null.
- Added tests

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/53451

issue_context.title: StreamPipeReader.ReadAsync() throws a NullReferenceException when CancelPendingRead() is called during a zero-byte read
issue_context.body:

Mac OS: Big Sur(11.4)
.NET 6 SDK: 6.0.100-preview.5.21277.7(runtime 6.0.0-preview.5.21276.11)

On windows7, this issue also repro, but not repro on win10.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46206739/119966638-17ed3a80-bfde-11eb-9c6a-a58c3d357f09.png)
@BrennanConroy  can you please look into this? Looks like this is preview5 blocker.
Also tagging @halter73 and @Tratcher in case Brennan isn't around today.

Thanks for the report. I was able to reproduce this.

It looks like this is an issue with Kestrel's shutdown logic triggering a call to StreamPipeReader.CancelPendingRead() during a zero byte read. This causes the StreamPipeReader to [trigger an internal CancellationTokenSource](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7cb1017813183fb51adba5e6fea6e4bf89a7848c/src/libraries/System.IO.Pipelines/src/System/IO/Pipelines/StreamPipeReader.cs#L163) which causes the zero byte read to throw an OperationCancellationException (or at least on macOS and Windows 7 it does apparently).

[Here's the relevant part](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7cb1017813183fb51adba5e6fea6e4bf89a7848c/src/libraries/System.IO.Pipelines/src/System/IO/Pipelines/StreamPipeReader.cs#L228-L266) of the ReadAsync call that is throwing the NullReferenceException. Since the call to `...InnerStream.ReadAsync(...` happens before `reader.AllocateReadTail();` and the `// Catch cancellation and translate it into setting isCanceled = true` branch in the catch swallows the exception, ReadAsync now tries to construct a ReadResult with a null `_readTail`.

This is a regression in StreamPipeReader introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/49117.

I debugged this on Windows10, and the 0-byte read just completes without throwing returning 0 when the CancellationToken fires. I find that unexpected @wfurt. 

The text of the NullReferenceException for reference.

```
warn: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel[0]
      Connection processing ended abnormally.
      System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
         at System.IO.Pipelines.StreamPipeReader.GetCurrentReadOnlySequence() in System.IO.Pipelines.dll:token 0x6000123+0x0
         at System.IO.Pipelines.StreamPipeReader.<ReadAsync>g__Core|36_0(StreamPipeReader reader, CancellationTokenSource tokenSource, CancellationToken cancellationToken) in System.IO.Pipelines.dll:token 0x600012a+0x0
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.Internal.Http.HttpProtocol.ProcessRequests[TContext](IHttpApplication`1 application) in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll:token 0x6000d24+0xd3
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.Internal.Http.HttpProtocol.ProcessRequestsAsync[TContext](IHttpApplication`1 application) in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.dll:token 0x6000d23+0x87
```

I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

> I find that unexpected @wfurt.

I assume from your mentioning Tomas that the underlying stream is an SslStream? What kind of Stream is it in turn wrapping?
Well, it's an SslStream wrapping our own Stream in Kestrel, so it might be our stream as well.

> so it might be our stream as well

Right,  I was asking what the SslStream is wrapping. It's delegating to the inner stream at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/c6b5994fbc251ef99c90ed05ce8b10059778e7cd/src/libraries/System.Net.Security/src/System/Net/Security/SslStream.Implementation.cs#L797; if the token had cancelation requested, I'd have expected that to throw.

> Yah

I assume that `_throwOnCancelled` is false and that's why it's returning 0 rather than throwing?

`_throwOnCancelled` should only affect `PipeReader.CancelPendingRead()`/`ReadResult.IsCanceled`. It shouldn't affect what happens given a canceled token imo. Looking at the code, it looks like the CancellationToken is flowed to the underlying Stream and I don't see anything catching an OperationCanceledException. It's not necessarily an SslStream issue though. It could also be something to do with Kestrel's Socket transport.
